items.q: Is "mind-body connection" just a metaphor for Langer?
items.a: No — **mind and body are one system**, tested empirically across **50 years**. Framing, noticing, and expecting change vision, hearing, strength, weight, blood pressure, wound healing, nursing-home mortality, and **biological aging markers**.

items.q: How is Langer mindfulness different from meditation?
items.a: **Mindfulness ≠ meditation**. Meditation may produce post-meditative mindfulness; Langer's version is a **way of being** — when you know you don't know, you pay attention; when you pay attention, **choices appear** that were invisible before.

items.q: What happened in the counterclockwise aging study?
items.a: Elderly men lived one week in a **1959-retrofitted retreat** as their younger selves — **vision, hearing, memory, strength, and appearance** improved in under a week via environment plus psychological framing.

items.q: Can trivial choices really extend life?
items.a: 1970s **nursing-home choice** study: movie Tuesday vs Thursday, or caring for a plant — residents with trivial autonomy showed an **18-month survival advantage**.

items.q: How did hotel maids lose weight without working harder?
items.a: Chambermaids told their work **counts as exercise** lost weight and lowered blood pressure with **no behavior change** — a nocebo-of-hidden-exercise demonstration: they already exercised but didn't *know* it.

items.q: How do doctors' timelines affect healing?
items.a: Wounds heal on the **doctor's stated timeline**. Saying "we don't know — some heal faster" preserves faster options; a fixed "it will take a month" **organizes the body** differently.

items.q: Can expectation change vision on an eye chart?
items.a: Standard Snellen charts that shrink letters **prime failure**. Reversing expectation let people **read lines they couldn't before** — vision follows expectation.
Yes — a **poison-ivy rash** can follow belief about the leaf, not just chemistry; ipecac can **stop vomiting** when labeled as anti-nausea.
Bottom-up: actively notice **three new things** about someone you live with, or on each walk — reveals how little you knew the "familiar" and fights **mindlessness**.
Top-down: everything was once a **human decision** — weight limits, timelines, diagnoses. Putting people back in the equation makes social facts **mutable** again.

items.q: Why doesn't going to bed early for a 4:30 AM flight work?
items.a: **Sleep need is retrospective** — it follows *yesterday's* activity, not tomorrow's alarm. Early-flight sleep paradox: last night's load sets tonight's requirement.
Air Florida: warm-climate pilots ran an **anti-ice-off checklist** in DC snow. **Mindful checklists** require fresh attention on each item — rote procedures kill.

items.q: How does Langer link burnout to mindlessness?
items.a: Treating each patient visit as **identical** is exhausting; noticing what's **new in the same person** is energizing — burnout as mindlessness, not just workload.
